It starts a server and serves the client API. 17 Read more about [How the Hoodie server works](server). 18 19 A good place to start is our [Tracker App](https://github.com/hoodiehq/hoodie-app-tracker). 20 You can play around with Hoodie’s APIs in the browser console and see how it 21 works all together in its [simple HTML and JavaScript code](https://github.com/hoodiehq/hoodie-app-tracker/tree/master/public). 22 23 If you have any questions come and say hi in our [chat](http://hood.ie/chat/). 24 25 ## Setup 26 27 This setup is working for all operating system, testing on Windows 8, Windows 8.1, Windows 10, Mac and Linux. 28 29 Hoodie is a [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/) package. You need Node Version 4 30 or higher and npm Version 2 or higher, check your installed version with `node -v` and `npm -v`. 31 32 First, create a folder and a [package.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/files/package.json) file 33 34 ``` 35 mkdir my-app 36 cd my-app 37 npm init -y 38 ``` 39 40 Next, install hoodie and save it as dependency 41 42 ``` 43 npm install --save hoodie 44 ``` 45 46 Now start up your Hoodie app 47 48 ``` 49 npm start 50 ``` 51 52 You can find a more thorough description in our [Getting Started Guide](http://docs.hood.ie/en/latest/guides/quickstart.html). 53 54 ## Usage 55 56 `hoodie` can be used standalone or as a [hapi plugin](http://hapijs.com/tutorials/plugins). 57 The options are slightly different. For the standalone usage, see [Hoodie’s configuration guide](http://docs.hood.ie/en/latest/guides/configuration.html). 58 For the hapi plugin usage, see [Hoodie’s hapi plugin usage guide](http://docs.hood.ie/en/latest/guides/hapi-plugin.html). 59 60 ## Testing 61 62 Local setup 63 64 ``` 65 git clone https://github.com/hoodiehq/hoodie.git 66 cd hoodie 67 npm install 68 ``` 69 70 The `hoodie` test suite is run with `npm test`. 71 You can [read more about testing Hoodie](test). 72 73 You can start hoodie itself by using `npm start`.
